subject: [PATCH v4 00/21] iomap: convert to in-iter iomap_next() model

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed a concern about the iomap_iter() logic, moved it out into an inlined helper function called iomap_iter_next(), and provided macros to generate boilerplate ->iomap_next() wrapper functions. No functional change intended.

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the pending iomap_iter_next conversion creates performance issues for the new simple direct I/O read fast path, agreed to split the simple path from iomap_dio_rw and require file systems to call into it explicitly, and pass only a ->begin callback. This will allow dropping various checks for incompatible features while creating a requirement for the file system to only call the simple path for cases that it can handle.

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed a concern about GFP_KERNEL allocation in non-blocking iocbs, agreed to switch to GFP_NOWAIT allocation instead.

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the fallback path for filesystems that don't provide an ->iomap_next() callback, explaining that iomap_iter() will fall back to the ->iomap_begin()/->iomap_end() path. The author's response suggests no immediate fix or revision needed.
reviews.raw_body:
Have one ->iomap_next() callback instead of ->iomap_begin() and
->iomap_end(). ->iomap_next() finishes the previous mapping if needed,
and produces the next mapping.

Collapsing to a single callback lets a performance-critical caller
inline its iteration loop and pass its ->iomap_next() function as a
compile-time constant, so the compiler can devirtualize that callback
into a direct call instead of an indirect call through a function
pointer.

iomap_iter() uses ->iomap_next() when the filesystem provides that
callback and otherwise falls back to the ->iomap_begin()/->iomap_end()
path, so filesystems can be converted one at a time.

Suggested-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Suggested-by: Matthew Wilcox (Oracle) <willy@infradead.org>
Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Signed-off-by: Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com>
---
 fs/iomap/iter.c       | 8 ++++++--
 include/linux/iomap.h | 9 +++++++++
 2 files changed, 15 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/fs/iomap/iter.c b/fs/iomap/iter.c
index 66ccb87441ab..e05574602946 100644
--- a/fs/iomap/iter.c
+++ b/fs/iomap/iter.c
@@ -107,8 +107,12 @@ int iomap_iter(struct iomap_iter *iter, const struct iomap_ops *ops)
 
 	trace_iomap_iter(iter, ops, _RET_IP_);
 
-	ret = iomap_iter_next(iter, &iter->iomap, &iter->srcmap,
-			ops->iomap_begin, ops->iomap_end);
+	if (ops->iomap_next)
+		ret = ops->iomap_next(iter, &iter->iomap, &iter->srcmap);
+	else
+		ret = iomap_iter_next(iter, &iter->iomap, &iter->srcmap,
+				ops->iomap_begin, ops->iomap_end);
+
 	iter->status = 0;
 	if (ret > 0)
 		iomap_iter_done(iter);
diff --git a/include/linux/iomap.h b/include/linux/iomap.h
index 80832edc7ec2..d203d9fe0f89 100644
--- a/include/linux/iomap.h
+++ b/include/linux/iomap.h
@@ -231,9 +231,18 @@ typedef int (*iomap_iter_begin_fn)(struct inode *inode, loff_t pos,
 typedef int (*iomap_iter_end_fn)(struct inode *inode, loff_t pos, loff_t length,
 		ssize_t written, unsigned flags, struct iomap *iomap);
 
+/*
+ * Produce the next mapping (finishing the previous one if needed).
+ * Return 1 to continue iterating, 0 if the range is fully consumed, or a
+ * negative error on failure.
+ */
+typedef int (*iomap_iter_next_fn)(const struct iomap_iter *iter,
+		struct iomap *iomap, struct iomap *srcmap);
+
 struct iomap_ops {
 	iomap_iter_begin_fn iomap_begin;
 	iomap_iter_end_fn iomap_end;
+	iomap_iter_next_fn iomap_next;
 };
 
 /**
--

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the retry mechanism in xfs's iomap operations, specifically that it relies on the ->iomap_begin method returning -ENOPROTOOPT. The author explained that this is actually based on the ->iomap_next method returning -ENOPROTOOPT and provided updated code to reflect this change.

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the implementation of the ->iomap_next() callback in the btrfs filesystem, explaining that it is generated by the DEFINE_IOMAP_ITER_NEXT_END() macro and does not introduce any functional changes.
reviews.raw_body:
Convert btrfs iomap_ops to the new ->iomap_next() callback. The callback is
generated with the DEFINE_IOMAP_ITER_NEXT_END() macro, which wraps the
iomap_iter_next() helper to finish the previous mapping if needed and
produce the next one. No functional changes are intended.

Acked-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com>
---
 fs/btrfs/direct-io.c | 6 ++++--
 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/fs/btrfs/direct-io.c b/fs/btrfs/direct-io.c
index 460326d34143..d5439b06cdc9 100644
--- a/fs/btrfs/direct-io.c
+++ b/fs/btrfs/direct-io.c
@@ -798,9 +798,11 @@ static void btrfs_dio_submit_io(const struct iomap_iter *iter, struct bio *bio,
 	btrfs_submit_bbio(bbio, 0);
 }
 
+static DEFINE_IOMAP_ITER_NEXT_END(btrfs_dio_iomap_next, btrfs_dio_iomap_begin,
+				  btrfs_dio_iomap_end);
+
 static const struct iomap_ops btrfs_dio_iomap_ops = {
-	.iomap_begin            = btrfs_dio_iomap_begin,
-	.iomap_end              = btrfs_dio_iomap_end,
+	.iomap_next             = btrfs_dio_iomap_next,
 };
 
 static const struct iomap_dio_ops btrfs_dio_ops = {
--

2026-07-27.patch_summary: This patch series converts the iomap code to use an iterator model, replacing the current begin/end pair of callbacks with a single next callback. This change allows for improved performance by enabling inlining and devirtualization of the iteration loop, as well as providing more flexibility for future callers to express custom logic in the IO path. The patches are broken down into 21 steps, including refactoring existing code, adding the new next callback, converting each filesystem, removing legacy paths, and updating documentation.

reviews.raw_body:

reviews.author: Brian Foster
reviews.summary: Reviewer Brian Foster expressed skepticism about the practical impact of a potential error path in xfs_bmbt_to_iomap(), suggesting that it's unlikely to occur due to earlier validation, and requested further review before posting the patch.
reviews.raw_body:
Sounds good to me, I'll post the current patch shortly.

I don't think anybody is actually hitting this in reality; it just came
from a Sashiko review. I had an LLM walk through and try and tell me
what error paths could lead to this in practice and it basically
narrowed it down to the startblock check in xfs_bmbt_to_iomap(). When
pressed further from there, it says this is mutually exclusive with a
populated batch in practice due to earlier validation at the time the
extents are read in from disk.

I'm not sure I trust the analysis with 100% certainty, but all in all it
seems like an unlikely or second order (i.e. memory corruption, etc.)
error scenario.

Brian
